One desk lamp. A student slumped over a laptop, surrounded by crumpled paper and empty cups. On screen, a spinning loader: AI THINKING… It's been thinking for hours. The fan inside the laptop screams, hot air pouring out. The room is sweltering.
On the desk: a single glass of water. The last one. His throat is dry — he reaches for it.
Close on his face. He stops. Looks at the glass. Looks at the overheating, struggling machine. The loader stutters — the AI is about to thermal-throttle, about to give up right when he needs the answer.
A choice. His thirst, or the machine's.
Slow, deliberate. He lifts the glass — and instead of drinking, he pours it into the machine. The water flows over the circuits and, impossibly, the heat breaks. Steam lifts. The fan quiets. The screen cools from angry red to calm blue.
The loader resolves. SOLUTION FOUND.
He sits back, exhausted, victorious — and parched. He's traded his own water to cool the machine that will save everyone else's.
Text fades in: "We're already pouring our water into our machines. We just don't see the glass."
Hard cut — the bigger picture. Pull back: that single glass becomes millions of liters, the dorm becomes a data center drinking a city's water supply to stay cool. The student's small sacrifice, multiplied across the planet.
